def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    path = "data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/2024_CSN_State_Rankings_Fraud_and_Other_Reports.csv"
    # File has a title row then true header on the next line.
    df = pd.read_csv(path, encoding="latin1", header=1, skip_blank_lines=True)
    # Some files still include an extra header row as first data row; drop it if present.
    if len(df) > 0 and str(df.iloc[0, 0]).strip() == "Rank":
        df = df.iloc[1:].reset_index(drop=True)
    return df

def process(fraudOtherReports, identityTheftReports) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    def normalize(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        df = df.copy()
        # Standardize expected columns if present
        # Handle possible unnamed columns by mapping first four columns.
        if all(c.startswith("Unnamed") for c in df.columns[:4]):
            df.columns = ["Rank", "State", "Reports per 100K Population", "# of Reports"]
        # Drop duplicated header row if it exists
        if len(df) > 0 and str(df.iloc[0].get("Rank", "")).strip() == "Rank":
            df = df.iloc[1:].reset_index(drop=True)
        # Keep only valid state rows
        df = df[df["State"].notna() & df["Reports per 100K Population"].notna()]
        # Clean numeric density
        df["Reports per 100K Population"] = (
            df["Reports per 100K Population"].astype(str).str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
        )
        df["density"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Reports per 100K Population"], errors="coerce")
        df = df[df["density"].notna()]
        return df[["State", "density"]]

    f = normalize(fraudOtherReports)
    i = normalize(identityTheftReports)

    total = (
        pd.concat([f, i], ignore_index=True)
        .groupby("State", as_index=False)["density"].sum()
        .sort_values("density", ascending=False)
    )

    return total.head(1)

operators.customDisplayName: Normalize both Fraud & Other Reports and Identity Theft Reports tables to columns ['State','density'] (rename Unnamed columns to ['Rank','State','Reports per 100K Population','# of Reports'] when needed; drop duplicated header rows; drop non-data/source/blank rows; parse 'Reports per 100K Population' removing commas; coerce to numeric). Concatenate categories and groupby State summing densities (reports per 100K are additive across report types). Sort by summed density descending and return top-1 state.
